root_idea.summary: The root is oriented around the left-hand side or direction.
root_idea.development: From the left-side orientation, the lexicon develops related geographical senses for al-Shām and the northern region, as well as figurative senses of ill fortune and inauspiciousness.

qac_form_accounting.reason: A Quran-attested nominal form with an independently supported lexical meaning and a normalized citation headword.

senses.definition: The left side, direction, or relative location.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction أصحاب المشأمة, the word has a literal spatial association with the left side or direction.

senses.definition: The occupants of the left; those whose records are given into their left hands.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic designation in أصحاب المشأمة, contrasted with أصحاب الميمنة and understood as referring to those assigned to the left or receiving their records in their left hands.

senses.definition: The occupants of a low or ignoble station.
senses.usage_conditions: An explicitly reported interpretive reading of أصحاب المشأمة in the Quranic passages where the expression occurs.

senses.definition: Those characterized by misfortune or ill fortune.
senses.usage_conditions: An explicitly reported interpretive reading of أصحاب المشأمة, connecting the designation with unfortunateness rather than merely physical leftness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become unlucky; to cause ill fortune to befall someone; or to regard someone or something as an evil omen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence includes constructions with عَلَى and بِهِ, including finding a person or thing unlucky, becoming unlucky through it, and auguring evil from it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unluckiness, inauspiciousness, ill fortune, or an evil omen; more generally, evil or misfortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal expression for the state or consequence of being unlucky, opposed to good fortune; it can also denote an evil omen or a cause of unluckiness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take the direction of the left hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A directional construction, opposed to taking the direction of the right hand.
A Form IV usage contrasted with أَيْمَنَ, to desire the right.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go to or come to al-Shām, or to send or direct someone there.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence includes both intransitive movement toward Syria and causing others to journey there, as well as taking the direction of al-Shām.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To assert a relationship to the people of al-Shām.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form V usage concerning claimed affiliation with the people of Syria.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Al-Shām, the country or region known as Syria; by extension, the northern region.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The geographical sense may be used for the northern region of Arabia, contrasted with al-Yaman to the south.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mole on a person's body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a separate nominal usage from the directional and ill-fortune senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Nature, innate disposition, temperament, or another inherent quality.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The pronunciation with hamza is reported, though its status is treated as unusual by one authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Syrian; of or relating to al-Shām; northern.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine forms apply to a woman or feminine referent, and the geographical adjective is normally formed without retaining the hamza of the country name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most unlucky, inauspicious, or unfortunate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be used substantively in the sense of شُؤْمٌ; in a poetic expression it characterizes boys as bearers of ill luck, and in a proverb an expression with this form is explained idiomatically of the tongue.
A lexicalized directional adjective, opposed to أَيْمَنُ and equivalent in this use to الشِّمَالُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unlucky or inauspicious; bringing ill fortune; an unlucky omen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as both an epithet and a substantive, of a person or thing and of an omen; plural forms are also reported.
Reported as a plural without a singular by some authorities; another analysis treats the form as شِيمٌ, the plural of أَشْيَمُ.

cautions: The Quranic expression أصحاب المشأمة is explicitly given several interpretive readings: literal leftness, receipt of records in the left hand, low or ignoble station, and unfortunateness. These are retained as distinct Quran-attested senses rather than treated as interchangeable contextual glosses.
